title: Lieb-Thirring eigenvalue bound for 2cosh(bP)-V with nonnegative integrable V and lower bound at minus two
author: Ari Laptev; Lukas Schimmer
source_title: A Sharp Lieb-Thirring Inequality for Functional Difference Operators
difficulty_reason: The author obtains a spectral-weight bound using a normalized functional-difference resolvent rather than the ordinary differential comparison bound. The new kernel has a convolution property that yields majorization of the Birman-Schwinger operators; a cumulative eigenvalue argument then gives the full summability estimate with multiplicities. Positivity fails outside the specified spectral regime, making the lower-bound hypothesis essential.
source_version: Official SIGMA 17 (2021) article 105, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2021.105; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Read the free functional-difference resolvent calculation, the normalized kernel Fourier probability measure and convolution identity, Lemma3.3 full majorization construction, and Section3.2 cumulative eigenvalue/trace proof. Ky Fan/Birman-Schwinger facts and the short general majorization lemma quoted with attribution to [6] are prior background; the operator-specific convolution and trace argument are supplied in full. Select only inequality(1.2). Section4 attains equality for a separately defined Dirac point interaction, which is not an L1 function; no equality-attainment assertion for L1 potentials is included, and no separate point-interaction helper is counted.

statement_scope: The inequality(1.2) part of Theorem1.1 only: b>0, P=-i d/dx on L2(R), W_V(b) the Friedrichs form realization of 2cosh(bP)-V, V>=0 in L1(R), and W_V(b)>=-2. For discrete eigenvalues lambda_j=-2cos(omega_j) in [-2,2), repeated with multiplicity, sum sin(omega_j)/omega_j <= (2pi b)^(-1) integral V. At omega=0 use the continuous ratio. The subsequent sharpness/equality sentence is excluded because the author equality example is a Dirac point interaction, outside L1.
